head: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents buy things for you after you approve
dek: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November, a payment feature that lets its Dots agents shop for you: you save a card once, and you approve every purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint. It starts with ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are over 18.
details: It was built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa and takes US-issued cards from those three. The Dot never sees your card number: each purchase gets a payment token that works for that one transaction, and each purchase leaves a record. OpenAI says card rewards and protections for eligible disputes stay as they are, and it takes no cut of purchases at launch. Some sellers keep agents out: Amazon blocks them, and United Airlines said on 11 November it will block agents from booking tickets.
where: US, ChatGPT Pro subscribers over 18, with a US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card
means: If you pay for ChatGPT Pro, your Dot can now take a purchase through to checkout, but nothing is bought until you review the items, see the total and approve it.
todo: Check the items and the total before you approve each purchase. If you'd rather not store a card in ChatGPT, you don't have to: the feature only works once you add one.
thumb_words: CHATGPT CAN NOW BUY THINGS FOR YOU
